notes: Analyst pass, iteration 2: (1) With-skill 17/17 (100%), baseline 16/17 (95%). Iteration-1 fixes verified in behavior: eval-0 with-skill committed to one primary with a flip condition on the runner-up (new decisiveness rule), used exact plugin-prefixed names, and eval-1/2/3 with-skill runs all produced the new Blockers line — eval-1 even caught that src/stats.py doesn't exist. (2) The only failure is the intended discriminator: eval-0 baseline again hedged ('Alternative driver… pick one driver, not both'), confirming decisiveness is skill-induced, not model-default. (3) Routing nondeterminism observed: eval-0 with-skill picked taste-skill:redesign-skill this iteration vs design-master in iteration 1 — the 'specificity wins' and 'explicit claim wins' heuristics pull opposite ways for this pair. Both picks are defensible and both were committed with stated flip conditions, so treated as acceptable variance, but a user wanting stable routing could add a tie-priority note to the heuristics. (4) Baseline improved vs iteration 1 on blocker-flagging without prompting (eval-2, eval-3) — that assertion no longer discriminates; the decisiveness assertion is now the load-bearing one. (5) With-skill overhead steady at ~3-4k tokens and ~15-20s per run for reading SKILL.md + heuristics.
